subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 — SDK backoff suspected
messages:
From: Olivia Martinez <olivia.martinez@streamline.com>
To: support@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in 5xx/429 across production — urgent

Hi team,

We started seeing a sharp escalation in 5xx/429 responses and client-side timeouts starting ~11:30 PDT yesterday. Latency for our critical payment path jumped from p95 ~120ms to 2.4s, and retries from the client exploded. Attached is a short traffic snapshot (traffic-graphs.png) and a tail of our client logs showing repeated attempts.

This is impacting settled transactions and has triggered our ops page. We believe it may be related to the latest SDK we rolled (v2.3.1) but need help confirming root cause and an immediate mitigation we can apply on our side. Can someone join an incident call in the next 30 minutes?

What I can provide now:
- SDK version: 2.3.1 (default retry policy)
- Approx traffic: 1.2k rps to Redwood endpoint; peak burst ~4k rps
- Samples of failing requests and timestamps attached

Please escalate — our CS execs are on standby.

Thanks,
Olivia Martinez
Senior SRE
Streamline Payments
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Martinez <olivia.martinez@streamline.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 across production — urgent

Hi Olivia — thanks for the heads up and attachments. I saw the graphs; that ramp looks very sharp.

Ben and Markus — looping you in for triage. Can you confirm whether we've observed regional saturation or a policy-induced retry amplification?

Immediate ask for Streamline: can you share the SDK retry configuration (backoff type, initial delay, max attempts)? If you can paste the retry block or attach the config, that will speed things up.

Olivia — we can join a short call now; I can host. Next steps on the call: quick mitigation guidance you can apply, and we’ll propose a short-term platform mitigation if needed.

—Grace
Grace O’Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: olivia.martinez@streamline.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 across production — urgent

Quick triage notes (initial):
- I pulled the telemetry and the error surge maps 1:1 to the client-side retry bursts. Support log tail attached (support-log-tail.txt).
- Pattern: circular amplification — client attempts returned 429/503, client retried with near-zero jitter/exponential not configured (looks like fixed delays of 0/100/200ms), which created repeated bursts every ~300ms. That matches the ramp you sent.
- Endpoint load: per-region GPU queues hit steady 95%+ for 20+ min; queueing caused timeouts and 5xx generation.

Immediate remediation recommendations (customer-side):
1) Increase client backoff to full jitter exponential (recommended initial 100ms, max 2s, max attempts 6).
2) Patch SDK to v2.3.2 (we have a hotfix that changes the default retry to exponential+full-jitter). We can provide the patch and a one-line config change if you can deploy it.

Short-term platform mitigations we can apply now (we'll need to coordinate):
- Apply a temporary per-customer rate limit per token to smooth incoming bursts.
- Enable aggressive prefix/KV cache bypass for long-tail requests for the next 1h to reduce model compute pressure.

I'll be on the call and can push a throttling rule from our side if we have authorization.

—Ben
Senior Incident Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Martinez <olivia.martinez@streamline.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 across production — urgent

Olivia — follow-up from the call: we have a concrete short-term plan. Summary and M.A.P. (mutual action plan):

1) Immediate customer action (you):
 - Apply config tweak: set retry policy to exponential backoff with full jitter. Example (attach): customer-retry-config.yaml
 - Patch to SDK v2.3.2; if you can't deploy within 30 min, change the retry block as shown to reduce attempts to 6 and initial_delay 100ms.

2) Redwood immediate actions (we will):
 - Enable per-key soft throttling for your API keys for the next 60 minutes to smooth bursts (will not drop requests, just queue).
 - Monitor error rate and latency; roll back throttles when p95 latency < 250ms and 5xx < 0.5% for 15m window.
 - Prepare formal RCA and timeline for permanent SDK default change.

3) Executive coordination: if the mitigation doesn't stabilize within 2 hours, we will trigger an exec briefing and discuss SLA credit and deeper rate-limit measures.

Attachments: customer-retry-config.yaml (example).

Please confirm once you’ve applied the client change and we’ll flip the soft throttle.

Thanks — will keep you posted.
Grace
From: markus.klein@redwood.ai <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 17:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 across production — urgent

On Mon, Jun 29, 2026 at 09:36 PDT ben.carter@redwood.ai wrote:
> Quick triage notes (initial):
> - I pulled the telemetry and the error surge maps 1:1 to the client-side retry bursts.
> - Pattern: circular amplification — client attempts returned 429/503, client retried with near-zero jitter/exponential not configured...

Update from the platform side: we pushed the short-term mitigations last night at ~23:10 PDT:
- Soft per-key request pacing applied (token-based) for Streamline; this smoothed the burst and prevented queue saturation.
- Activated a compute-priority fallback: lower-cost model variant for non-critical paths to reduce GPU pressure.

Telemetry after mitigation:
- 5xx rate dropped from 6.8% -> 0.9% within 12 minutes of mitigation.
- p95 latency improved from 2.4s -> 180ms after 25 minutes.

Next steps (RCA path):
- Change default SDK retry policy to exponential+full-jitter and ship in 2 weeks (v2.4.0).
- Backfill tests in SDK e2e harness to detect aggressive fixed-delay retries.
- Formal RCA write-up and timeline for customer-facing postmortem (target: 2026-07-07).

Rishi — flagging this for exec visibility given the impact on a high-value account and the potential need for a formal sales credit discussion.

—Markus
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
